competency_fulfillment.rationale: All thirteen seeds carry the single stem 'Are Segment A and Segment B equal in length?' with both lengths already printed, for example seed 42 'Segment A is 2 cm long. Segment B is 2 cm long.' keyed 'Yes' and seed 44 'Segment A is 7 cm long. Segment B is 3 cm long.' keyed 'No'. Every item is answerable from what its stem says, but of the two verbs the sentence names only identify is touched, and only in a reduced numeral-comparison form; draw is absent from the whole pool, since no seed asks the student to draw or construct a segment of a stated length.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Coverage is limited to one yes/no equality judgment. Equal pairs (seeds 42, 43, 45, 46, 501, 502, 602, 604) and unequal pairs (seeds 44, 50, 500, 601, 603) are both represented and the keys 'Yes' and 'No' are reasonably balanced, but there is no construction task, no ruler-reading task, and no item that presents segments to be identified rather than described in words, so roughly half the competency is unrepresented.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Nothing exceeds the Grade 3 Quarter 1 ceiling: no conversion, no formula, no later-grade vocabulary. The problem runs the other way. With both lengths given in the stem, seed 603 'Segment A is 3 cm long. Segment B is 4 cm long.' reduces to deciding whether 3 and 4 are the same number, a judgment available well before Grade 3, and no seed requires a student to align, read or set a ruler.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: One template serves all thirteen seeds. Seed 42 and seed 46 are the identical item, both 'Segment A is 2 cm long. Segment B is 2 cm long. Are Segment A and Segment B equal in length?' keyed 'Yes'. The formatter label alternates between mcq and cloze, but the stem wording, the option set and the required task never change, so the student meets one question repeated with different numbers.

competency_alignment.rationale: Nothing drifts outside the topic of segment length, so there is no over-reach, but the mapping is only partial. The sentence names drawing with a ruler and no seed produces or demands either action. Seed 500 'Segment A is 60 cm long. Segment B is 65 cm long.' hands the student both measurements outright, which is representative of the whole pool: the ruler named in the competency has no role in any of the thirteen items.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Several segments cannot be drawn or checked with the ruler the sentence names. Seed 604 uses 'Segment A is 2 m long. Segment B is 2 m long.', a two-metre line segment, and seeds 500, 501 and 502 use 60, 65 and 82 cm, all past a classroom ruler, which measures well under a metre, and past the width of a worksheet. The 1 to 8 cm seeds (42, 43, 44, 45, 46, 50, 601, 602, 603) are appropriate. Only line segments appear, so no triangle inequality question arises.
